title: Residual run_id gaps after the cycle-1571 H1 fix — fanout writer, dead Runner, and a TRAP on worktree_tree_sha
summary: Follow-ups from the architect review of the H1-H4 PR. (a) DANGEROUS — DO NOT DO NAIVELY: subagent/run.go's auditor entry carries no worktree_tree_sha, so ship falls back to the auditor's prose audit_bound_tree_sha, which ship/audit.go:117-128 documents as guaranteeing INTEGRITY_TREE_DRIFT (cycle-152). The obvious fix (stamp worktree_tree_sha there) would SILENTLY RE-OPEN cycle-1571 H4: the release preflight distinguishes a manual release audit from a cycle audit precisely BY that field's absence, so stamping it makes manual release audits indistinguishable from lane audits and restores the false veto. Any fix must handle both invariants together, or document the TREE_DRIFT constraint instead. (b) subagent/helpers.go's agent_fanout writer carries no run_id, so per-run ledger attribution stays partial under fleet concurrency. (c) subagent.Runner (subagent.go:123-288) appears production-dead — cmd_subagent.go is the package's only non-test importer and never calls New; either delete it (it duplicates run.go's dispatch, §3.5) or annotate it unreachable and correct the guard map's description. (d) Upgrade ledger_runid_writers_guard_test.go to go/ast so constant indirection (Kind: kindSubprocess), assignment form (e.Kind = ...), and split literal/construction sites cannot evade it; widen scan roots beyond internal+cmd and scan git-tracked files.
